title: Review of the fuel-powered CIPS division finding on fresh seed 7: the cells still divide with the enzyme turnover charged to the fuel (7 persistent splits, layered daughters, 0 merges), but only to generation 1 and with no delay against the fuel-independent control (first splits t=2600 vs 2500)
summary: labkit re-runs at the finding's settings (192^2, t=12000, default window) on seed 7: fuel-powered turnover (defaults) 17 bodies at the end, 7 persistent splits (t=2600-8000), max generation 1, 0 merges, 8 nucleations, s rim membrane-like on all four top tracks; the matched fuel-independent reactivation (react_const 1) 16 bodies, 7 persistent splits (t=2500-4700), generation 1, 0 merges. The sheets show the same pinching of elongated layered cells into two round daughters in both arms (pack/sheet.png t=2100-3600, t=9900).

observations.D: pack/sheet.png t=2100-3600: elongated layered cells pinch into two round daughters with the turnover paid by fuel; 7 persistent splits, 0 merges, generation 1 (pack/FACTS.md)

seeds_run.result: divides (7 persistent splits) but generation 1, not 2

controls_run.D: pack_const/ (react_const 1, seed 7): 7 persistent splits, generation 1, first split t=2500

verdicts.limitation: On my seed the daughters did not divide again within t=12000 (generation 1 from founders that nucleate from noise), and the fuel-powered arm divides as early and as often as the fuel-independent control (first split 2600 vs 2500, 7 vs 7), so the delay reported on seeds 0-1 (~500 t) and the slightly lower split count did not reproduce. I did not re-run the fuel fork, the moat or the flux budget. One seed.
